projects.name: FieldOps Mobile App
projects.description: Offline-first mobile application for field technicians, inspections, photos, and work order sync.
projects.objective: Deliver a source-backed app plan that separates mobile queue behavior, backend work-order ownership, and audit evidence.

nodes.title: Product scope
nodes.subtitle: Technician inspection workflow
nodes.notes: Technicians need assigned work orders, inspection checklist steps, barcode scanning, photo evidence, supervisor comments, and visible sync state.

nodes.title: Offline sync architecture
nodes.subtitle: Local queue and conflict decisions
nodes.notes: The mobile app owns a local mutation queue. The backend API remains the canonical owner of work order state. Idempotency keys are mandatory for each queued mutation.

nodes.title: Evidence storage
nodes.subtitle: Photos, notes, and upload retry
nodes.notes: Inspection photos must be attached to work order checkpoints. Failed uploads remain visible and retryable; the system must not silently drop technician notes or images.

nodes.title: Offline testing matrix
nodes.subtitle: Airplane mode, conflicts, and token expiry
nodes.notes: Test airplane mode, concurrent edit conflict, expired auth token during sync, partial photo upload, large image batch, and device storage exhaustion.

nodes.title: Operational telemetry
nodes.subtitle: Sync latency and failure visibility
nodes.notes: Metrics include sync latency, failed upload count, conflict count, retry attempts, queue age, and storage warnings. Logs must mask customer data.

nodes.title: Risk controls
nodes.subtitle: Audit and permissions
nodes.notes: Primary risks are ambiguous conflict resolution, photo upload loss, weak customer asset permissions, and missing audit history for offline edits.

projects.name: KnowledgeOps Dashboard
projects.description: Blazor support engineering dashboard for incident triage, runbook recall, and post-incident learning.
projects.objective: Build a dense operator tool that cites official sources and keeps generated memory review-gated.

nodes.title: Incident intake
nodes.subtitle: Severity, customer impact, owner
nodes.notes: The dashboard captures severity, affected customer, product area, current owner, symptom summary, and immediate mitigation state.

nodes.title: Runbook ranking
nodes.subtitle: Official source before generated summary
nodes.notes: Search must distinguish official runbooks from generated summaries. Memory-backed suggestions need source links and stale-runbook warnings.

nodes.title: Operator UI
nodes.subtitle: Dense, repeatable incident workflow
nodes.notes: Use compact lists, keyboard-friendly navigation, stable status badges, and action panels. Avoid marketing-style cards and decorative layouts.

nodes.title: Post-incident learning
nodes.subtitle: Review-gated memory proposals
nodes.notes: Postmortems, validated fixes, and regression proposals are captured as review-gated learning records, not direct truth mutation.

nodes.title: Source policy
nodes.subtitle: Citations and stale evidence
nodes.notes: Every suggested runbook needs a source reference. Stale or generated-only recommendations should be marked as caveated.

projects.documentHeading: Project C: ClinicFlow SaaS Business Plan
projects.name: ClinicFlow SaaS Business Plan
projects.description: Business plan for appointment reminders and no-show reduction in small clinics.
projects.objective: Validate a SaaS opportunity while separating product, go-to-market, compliance, and unit economics assumptions.

nodes.title: Market segment
nodes.subtitle: Small clinics with limited IT staffing
nodes.notes: Target independent clinics with 2-20 providers. Buyer is often a clinic manager or owner-operator; users include front desk staff and providers.

nodes.title: MVP scope
nodes.subtitle: Scheduling, reminders, no-show dashboard
nodes.notes: Avoid billing integrations in first pilot. Build schedule import, calendar view, reminder templates, no-show dashboard, and opt-out tracking.

nodes.title: Pricing hypothesis
nodes.subtitle: Per-provider subscription plus SMS pass-through
nodes.notes: Pricing hypothesis is provider-based subscription. SMS usage should be tracked separately to avoid margin surprises.

nodes.title: Compliance posture
nodes.subtitle: Privacy before pilot expansion
nodes.notes: Compliance and privacy posture must be explicit before pilots. Patient data handling, opt-out behavior, and retention must be documented.

nodes.title: Pilot plan
nodes.subtitle: Interviews before paid acquisition
nodes.notes: Start with clinic manager interviews, then a narrow pilot and case study. Broad paid advertising is not the first motion.

projects.documentHeading: Project D: Docker Development Platform Analysis
projects.name: Docker Development Platform Analysis
projects.description: Analysis of Docker usage for local dependencies, CI tests, and deployment parity boundaries.
projects.objective: Improve repeatability without hiding configuration failures or confusing local Compose with production architecture.

nodes.title: Local dependencies
nodes.subtitle: PostgreSQL, Redis, object storage mock
nodes.notes: Docker should standardize PostgreSQL, Redis, mail sink, and object storage mock startup for developers.

nodes.title: Compose profiles
nodes.subtitle: Core versus optional dependencies
nodes.notes: Compose profiles should separate core dependencies from optional heavyweight services. Health checks must expose failed startup states.

nodes.title: Build caching
nodes.subtitle: Fast restore and rebuild loops
nodes.notes: Image build caching matters for daily development. Restore layers, test image, and runtime image should be structured for stable cache reuse.

nodes.title: CI evidence
nodes.subtitle: Ephemeral DB and migration proof
nodes.notes: Test pipelines should use ephemeral databases, apply migrations explicitly, run API smoke checks, and tear down volumes.

nodes.title: Production parity boundary
nodes.subtitle: Local convenience is not deployment truth
nodes.notes: Production deployment decisions must not be inferred from local Compose convenience. Secrets, networking, readiness, and scaling differ.

projects.documentHeading: Project E: Regional Inflation And Small Business Economy Analysis
projects.name: Regional Inflation And Small Business Economy Analysis
projects.description: Non-programming economic analysis of inflation, credit, wages, and small business responses.
projects.objective: Separate observed indicators from scenarios and policy recommendations for regional small businesses.

nodes.title: Observed indicators
nodes.subtitle: Prices, wages, rates, credit spreads
nodes.notes: Track consumer prices, producer input costs, wage growth, credit spreads, default rates, rent, and business formation.

nodes.title: Business responses
nodes.subtitle: Inventory, hiring, pricing, debt caution
nodes.notes: Small businesses may preserve cash by reducing inventory depth, delaying expansion, adjusting pricing, and limiting new debt.

nodes.title: Sector split
nodes.subtitle: Retail, food service, trades, healthcare, logistics
nodes.notes: Analyze food service, retail, construction trades, healthcare services, and local logistics separately because margin and demand responses differ.

nodes.title: Scenarios
nodes.subtitle: Base, persistent inflation, credit crunch, rebound
nodes.notes: Forecasts need scenario labels and should not be mixed with observed indicators. Each scenario has different credit and demand assumptions.

nodes.title: Policy options
nodes.subtitle: Credit guarantees and local procurement
nodes.notes: Policy options include credit guarantees, targeted training, local procurement, and tax relief. Each must state tradeoffs and eligible sectors.

projects.name: Community Learning Program
projects.description: Non-programming adult education program for financial literacy, job search, and digital confidence.
projects.objective: Design modular community sessions with privacy-aware operations and measurable participant outcomes.

nodes.title: Learner needs
nodes.subtitle: Uneven schedules and varied digital skills
nodes.notes: Adults have uneven schedules, varied digital skills, and different comfort levels discussing money or job history.

nodes.title: Curriculum modules
nodes.subtitle: Budgeting, resume, interviews, account safety
nodes.notes: Modules include budgeting basics, avoiding predatory debt, resume refresh, interview practice, account safety, and benefits navigation.

nodes.title: Delivery model
nodes.subtitle: Short sessions with plain-language handouts
nodes.notes: Sessions should be short, modular, repeatable, and supported by printed handouts and phone-friendly reminders.

nodes.title: Partners
nodes.subtitle: Libraries, employers, nonprofits
nodes.notes: Libraries, local employers, and nonprofits reduce outreach cost and provide venue, referral, and facilitator support.

nodes.title: Evaluation
nodes.subtitle: Attendance, confidence, resumes, referrals
nodes.notes: Measure attendance, confidence surveys, completed resumes, budget plans, referral follow-through, and participant consent boundaries.
